text:
sara: Customer reports intermittent 200s and 500s from /v1/embeddings. Error text says 'vector dimension mismatch' on some requests. Started after a traffic bump ~0900 UTC. Can someone look?

mike: Can you paste a request id + sample logs? Is this only embeddings or other routes?

sara: Sample request id: req_0af9c2. Log snippet: 
```
ERROR EmbeddingBatcher - req=req_0af9c2 - built batch of 3 but produced vectors with lengths [768,512,768] - expected 768
WARN Runtime - model fallback to embed-small:v1 due to OOM on shard-7
```
Only embeddings route so far. Occurs in bursts during coalescing.

support_engineer_joe: This looks like dynbatch coalesced requests for two model variants (embed-large:v2 -> dim 768, embed-small:v1 -> dim 512). If a fallback happens while coalescing we sometimes end up mixing variants. Repro steps I used:
```
# quick repro (python)
for _ in range(30):
  requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={"input": "tiny text"}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer X","X-Model-Alias":"embed-large:v2"})
  time.sleep(0.02)
```
Trigger an OOM on one worker and you see mixed batches.

elaine: Confirming suspicion from runtime side: coalescer currently groups by route key but not by model variant when fallback routing happens. When a node preempts and returns fallback, the batch build path doesn't revalidate the variant per item. Adding variant isolation check should be safe.

infra-bot: [metrickey=embed.batch.error_rate] 09:02 -> 09:05 spike: 18% -> 52% on cluster embed-prod-us-east-1. Affected hosts: shard-7, shard-9.

mike: For immediate mitigation: set max_batch_size=1 or disable coalescing on the customer's route. That will kill throughput but stop mixed-dim responses. Also we can pin model_alias to embed-large:v2 for their api key.

sara: Customer is worried about being charged for bad vectors — some responses returned 200 but vector shape was wrong. Billing asked to confirm what we bill for.

billing-bot: Quick note: we bill for successful responses (2xx) per embedding unit. If vectors were malformed but response code 200, they were billed. We will mark refunds/credits per affected request ids once we get a list.

support_engineer_joe: I pulled a small list of affected req ids from logs: [req_0af9c2, req_0af9c8, req_0afa11]. Please flag these for credit and set a short-term rule: if vector length != model expected dim then return 5xx instead of 200.

elaine: Patch incoming: PR #repo/runtime/changeset 652a3f — adds variant-aware coalescing key and a guard that validates produced dims before returning 200. If mismatch, we drop batch and retry with per-request routing. Plan: backport to 1.12.x and roll to prod tonight in a canary.

mike: Operational playbook: 1) Pin customer to embed-large:v2, 2) set max_batch_size=1 for their route, 3) monitor error rate for 30m, 4) apply PR and roll canary.

sara: I've communicated mitigations. Customer accepted temporary throughput hit in exchange for correctness. I've asked billing to prepare credits.

billing-bot: Draft credit: full refund for affected requests and a one-week credit for any failed/slow requests tied to this incident. Will confirm amounts after list.

elaine: After deploy, follow-up tasks: add an alert for 'batch contains mixed model variants' (new metric), add unit test for fallback+coalesce, and document model-variant pinning option in docs/ops.

sara: Thanks all. I'll update customer and file an incident. Follow-up owners: runtime (elaine) PR/rollout, support (joe) customer creds, billing (billing-bot) refunds. Closing thread when canary is green. :thumbsup:
